# Introduction

Divers from the Northwest Fisheries Science Center (NWFSC) and the National Marine Sanctuaries (NMS) have conducted kelp-forest dive surveys in Olympic Coast National Marine Sanctuary (OCNMS) since 2015 (with the exception of 2020 due to COVID restrictions). Divers from the University of Washington and California State University Monterey Bay have participated as reciprocity divers. Surveys are completed at the end of July to beginning of August. In `r data_year`, surveys were competed between `r date_min` and `r date_max`.

In `r data_year`, divers completed `r fish_transects_year` fish transects, `r invert_transects_year` invertebrate transects, and `r algae_transects_year` across five (5) sites ([Fig. @fig-site-map]). After filtering the data for visibility (>2m), there were `r fish_transects_year2m` usable fish transects in `r data_year`. Divers recorded `r fish_taxa_year`, `r invert_taxa_year`, and `r algae_taxa_year` taxa of fish, invertebrates, and algae along these transects. To date (2015-`r data_year`), the survey has recorded `r fish_taxa_total`, `r invert_taxa_total`, and `r algae_taxa_total` taxa for fish, invertebrates, and algae.

# Methods

Divers on SCUBA conducted in situ surveys to count fish at each site along benthic belt transects (30 m by 2 m) following procedures modified from @malone2022large. Transects were conducted within or directly adjacent to canopy kelp beds (consisting of giant *Macrocystis pyrifera* or bull *Nereocystis luetkeana* kelps). In 2015 surveyed at 10 sites and conducted four (4) transects per site at 5 m depth ([Fig. @fig-site-map], [@shelton2018predictable]). From 2016 on, we surveyed at five (5) sites ([Fig. @fig-site-map]), sampling at two (2) locations within each site separated by \>100 m, and 2 depths within each location (5 and 10 m) Our goal was to complete six (6) replicate transects at each year-site-depth combination [@tolimieri2023changes].

```{r fig-site-map}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Dive survey locations in Olympic Coast National Marine Sanctuary along the coast of Washington State."

knitr::include_graphics( paste0(fig_dir,"site-map.png"))

```

During each fish transect, we counted and estimated the size (total length to nearest cm) of all fishes \>5 cm total length; the exception was rockfishes *Sebastes* spp., for which we estimated sizes of all individuals. Rockfishes $\leq$ 10 cm were considered young-of-year. Divers also estimated horizontal visibility on each transect by determining the distance at which the lead diver could distinguish their buddy's extended fingers. Transects with visibility less than 2 m were excluded from analyses.

## Divers / Data collectors

Many divers have contributed to the survey over the years. They include:

*Dive team in `r data_year`*: `r knitr::combine_words(divers2)`

*Dive team members:* `r knitr::combine_words(divers1)`

```{r prep-fish-effort}
#| echo: false

xfish = fish[fish$species=='OPEL',] 
tab_fish = xfish %>% group_by(year, site) %>% 
  summarize(N = n()) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols='site', names_from = year, values_from = N) %>%
  rename(Site = site)

```

Divers target 12 transects per site (3 transects x 2 locations x 2 depths), but are often able to complete additional transects on a dive (@tbl-fish-effort). In `r data_year` divers completed `r min(tab_fish[,ncol(tab_fish)], na.rm=T)`-`r max(tab_fish[,ncol(tab_fish)], na.rm=T)` 
for a total of `r sum(tab_fish[,ncol(tab_fish)], na.rm=T)` transects across all sites. Note, the analysts typically remove transects with visibility below 2.0 m for any investigation.

**why don't we have fish transects at Destruction Island in 2015**

### Adult fishes

Divers recorded `r nrow(Tspp)` adult fish taxa (@tbl-spp2). The most common species was `r Tspp$cn[1]` `r Tspp$Species[1]` with `r Tspp$Total[1]` counted to date.  The second most common species was `r Tspp$cn[2]` `r Tspp$species[2]`  `r Tspp$Total[2]`individuals observed by divers. In `r data_year` `r spp_yr_nm` was`text1`the most commonly recorded species with`r spp_yr_no` across the five sites.

```{r fish-text}

fish_taxa_Year_site <-  fish_transect %>% group_by(site,year,taxa) %>%
  summarise(Mean=mean(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD=sd(Count),
            N=length(Count),
            SE=SD/sqrt(N),
            SE_var=SE^2)

fish_taxa_year <-fish_taxa_Year_site %>% group_by(year,taxa) %>%
  summarise(grand_sum=sum(Mean, na.rm = TRUE),

text_black <- get_delta(dfile=fish_taxa_year, xtaxa="SEME", cname='black rockfish')

```

As noted black rockfish (*Sebastes melanostictus*) is the most commonly observed species in the dive survey (@fig-fish-year). `r text_black`. Greenlings are typically the second most observed taxa; these are primarily kelp greenlings *Hexagrammos decagrammus*, although the various species are lumped in Figure -@fig-fish-year.

### Rockfish young-of-year

It is difficult to visually distinguish many rockfish species when they are small. Therefore, on our surveys, we categorized juvenile rockfishes into five (5) groups established in the literature [@johansson2018seasonal; @markel2020contrasting]:

\(1\) Yellowtail and black (YTB) included both yellowtail (*S. flavidus*) and black (*S. melanops*) rockfishes

\(2\) The copper/quillback/brown (CQB) group included copper (*S. caurinus*), quillback (*S. maliger*), and brown (*S. auriculatus*) rockfishes

\(3\) Canary (*S. pinniger*)

\(4\) Blue rockfish (*S. mystinus*)

\(5\) Unidentified individuals were categorized as juvenile rockfishes

### Urchin trends

```{r prep-urchins}
tot_urchin_taxa_Year_site <-  invert %>% 
  filter(species %in% c('STRPUR','MESFRA','STRDRO')) %>%
  group_by(site,year) %>%
  summarise(Mean=mean(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD=sd(Count),
            N=length(Count),
            SE=SD/sqrt(N),
            SE_var=SE^2)

tot_urchin_taxa_year <-tot_urchin_taxa_Year_site %>% 
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(grand_sum=sum(Mean, na.rm = TRUE),
            N=length(Mean),
            xmean = mean(Mean),
            grand_mean= grand_sum / N,
            grand_sum_var =sum(SE_var, na.rm = TRUE), 
            grand_SE = sqrt(grand_sum_var / N^2)) %>%
  mutate(taxa='urchin')

text_urchin <- get_delta(dfile=tot_urchin_taxa_year, xtaxa="urchin", cname='total urchins')

# by spp
urchin_taxa_Year_site <-  invert %>% 
  filter(species %in% c('STRPUR','MESFRA','STRDRO')) %>%
  group_by(site,year,species) %>%
  summarise(Mean=mean(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD=sd(Count),
            N=length(Count),
            SE=SD/sqrt(N),
            SE_var=SE^2)

urchin_taxa_year <-urchin_taxa_Year_site %>% group_by(year,species) %>%
  summarise(grand_sum=sum(Mean, na.rm = TRUE),
            N=length(Mean),
            grand_mean= grand_sum / N,
            grand_sum_var =sum(SE_var, na.rm = TRUE), 
            grand_SE = sqrt(grand_sum_var / N^2)) %>%
  mutate(grand_mean = grand_mean)

text_purple <- get_delta(dfile=urchin_taxa_year, xtaxa="STRPUR", cname='purple urchins')

```
